Assemble the timeseries-level detail object for ctasapp drill-down

Combine_CTAS_Detail.Rd

Summarize_CTAS() collapses many timeseries into one row per group, which is what the gsm report needs and exactly what a reviewer investigating a flag does not: once a site is flagged, the next question is which measurement caused it. That question is answered by the ctasapp dashboard, so this function preserves the join keys the aggregation discards - timeseries_id, parameter_id and feature - in the shape ctasapp reads.

Usage

Combine_CTAS_Detail(dfScores, lInput, strStudyID = NULL)

Arguments

dfScores

data.frame Result of Combine_CTAS_Scores().

lInput

list Result of Combine_CTAS_Input(), the input to the same CTAS run.

strStudyID

character Optional study identifier.

Value

list with elements Results, Input and Untransformed.

Details

The division of labour is deliberate: the gsm report performs signal detection, ctasapp performs signal investigation. This is a parallel output of the same CTAS run, not a stage of the gsm pipeline - nothing downstream consumes it, and ctasapp does not consume the gsm reporting layer.

Three frames are returned, matching the files ctasapp accepts:

  • Results - one row per timeseries x feature x group, carrying site, timeseries_id, parameter_id, feature and fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp. This is Combine_CTAS_Scores() output unchanged, since that already satisfies the contract.

  • Input - the CTAS data frame joined to subjects and parameters, so the dashboard can plot the underlying series with site and parameter labels.

  • Untransformed - the pre-transformation values recorded by the Input_*() functions, letting the dashboard show a lab result in its original units alongside the range-normalised value actually analysed. Empty when no mapped domain records them.

strStudyID is optional and adds a study column to Results and Input; ctasapp uses it to hold several studies in one upload.

See also

Write_CTAS_Detail(), which writes these frames to disk in the layout ctasapp expects.

Examples

lInput <- Combine_CTAS_Input(
  Input_Numeric(data.frame(
    USUBJID = "S1", VSTESTCD = "SYSBP", VSTEST = "Systolic Blood Pressure",
    VISIT = "WEEK 2", VISITNUM = 3, VSSTRESN = 120
  )),
  dfSubjects = Input_Subjects(data.frame(
    USUBJID = "S1", SITEID = "701", COUNTRY = "USA"
  ))
)
dfScores <- data.frame(
  timeseries_id = "ts1", site = "701", feature = "average",
  parameter_id = "VS_SYSBP", fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp = 1.2
)
Combine_CTAS_Detail(dfScores, lInput)
#> $Results
#>   timeseries_id site feature parameter_id fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp
#> 1           ts1  701 average     VS_SYSBP                       1.2
#> 
#> $Input
#>   subject_id parameter_id timepoint_1_name timepoint_2_name timepoint_rank
#> 1         S1     VS_SYSBP           WEEK 2             <NA>              1
#>   result baseline site country region                       parameter_name
#> 1    120       NA  701     USA   <NA> Vital Signs: Systolic Blood Pressure
#>   parameter_category_1 parameter_category_2 parameter_category_3
#> 1          Vital Signs             VS_SYSBP              numeric
#> 
#> $Untransformed
#>   subject_id parameter_category_2 timepoint_1_name original_value lower upper
#> 1         S1             VS_SYSBP           WEEK 2            120    NA    NA
#>   original_category
#> 1              <NA>
#>
